input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an open-ended most-favoured-nation obligation on us: we must extend to Silverline terms no less favourable than the best terms we give any other technology supplier, with no product limitation, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. That is walk-away territory under the rule and it also contradicts Section 12.3, which states that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The only MFN mechanic in the document runs against us (nothing grants Customer best pricing), so we take the preferred position and remove the obligation, leaving Section 7.2 as an express confirmation that no Customer MFN applies.

ops.oldText: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the requirement that we give Silverline terms no less favourable than our best terms with any other technology supplier, since our playbook does not accept an MFN running against the Customer and this obligation contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Convert Section 7.2 from a Customer MFN obligation into an express confirmation that no such obligation exists.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
